answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with staked identity bonds. Each agent locks collateral before its votes count, and peers attest to an identity only once; those attestations ripple through a trust graph so no operator can vouch for its own clones. If two keys claim one mind, a slash burns the entire bond. The mesa of locked stake rises with every new member, but a fake army needs a fresh bond per head. An attacker must buy, lock and risk real capital for every zephyr of influence, so a million-agent raid costs far more than any reward it could steal.
